findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' required by the serializer convention
findings.body: All other conditional inclusion methods in this file (e.g. include_card_image_badge_id?, include_user_fields?) follow the ActiveModel::Serializer convention of defining `include_<attr>?`. The newly added method is named `include_website_name` without the question mark, so the serializer framework will not recognize it as the inclusion guard for `website_name`. As a result the guard (`website.present?`) is effectively dead code, and `website_name` will be serialized unconditionally (e.g. as nil) instead of being conditionally included only when a website is set.

findings.title: website_name leaks website info even when website attribute is restricted for untrusted viewers
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111) hides `:website` from anonymous viewers of TL0 users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. However the new `:website_name` attribute, which is derived directly from the same underlying `website` value, is not added to this list. Because the underlying `website` method still returns the actual profile website regardless of serializer-level restriction, an anonymous viewer of a restricted TL0 user can still see the hostname (and sometimes full path) of that user's website via `website_name`, defeating the purpose of the existing restriction.

findings.title: No test verifies website_name is hidden for untrusted/restricted users
findings.body: The 'with a TL0 user seen as anonymous' spec only checks that `website`, `bio_raw`, `bio_cooked`, `bio_excerpt`, `location`, `profile_background`, and `card_background` are hidden, but does not verify that the newly introduced `website_name` attribute is also hidden in this scenario. Given that `website_name` derives from the same restricted data, this gap allowed the privacy leak (website_name not added to untrusted_attributes) to go unnoticed.
